source_refs.note: Topic 10.14 with Figures 10.5 and 10.6, printed pages 227-228. Quick Check 10.6b is used in 10.17.3.

blocks.text: Three main types of half-cell have E standard values obtainable by connection to a standard hydrogen electrode: metal/metal ion (Cu2+/Cu), non-metal/non-metal ion (Cl2/Cl-) and ion/ion (Fe3+/Fe2+). Figure 10.5 shows the measurement for a Cu2+/Cu half-cell: connected to the SHE, the voltage is +0.34 V, copper being the positive terminal (positive pole) and the SHE the negative terminal. The half-equations are Cu2+(aq) + 2e- giving Cu(s), E standard = +0.34 V, and H+(aq) + e- giving 1/2 H2(g), E standard = 0.00 V. The values show that Cu2+ ions are easier to reduce than H+ ions (more positive E standard) and more likely to gain electrons, so Cu2+ accepts electrons from the H+/H2 half-cell and H2 loses electrons to the Cu2+/Cu half-cell.

Figure 10.6 shows the Zn2+/Zn half-cell: its voltage is -0.76 V, zinc being the negative terminal and the hydrogen electrode the positive terminal. The half-equations are H+ + e- giving 1/2 H2, 0.00 V, and Zn2+ + 2e- giving Zn, -0.76 V. Zn2+ ions are more difficult to reduce than H+ ions (more negative E standard) and less likely to gain electrons, so Zn loses electrons to the H+/H2 half-cell and H+ ions gain electrons from the Zn2+/Zn half-cell. From these two examples, reduction takes place at the positive terminal of the cell (in the Zn2+/Zn; H+/H2 cell: 2H+ + 2e- giving H2) and oxidation at the negative terminal (Zn giving Zn2+ + 2e-).

blocks.prompt: With E standard Cl2/2Cl- +1.36 V, Br2/2Br- +1.07 V and I2/2I- +0.54 V, explain why bromine oxidises iodide ions but does not react with chloride ions (Quick Check 10.6a).
blocks.explanation: The more positive the E standard, the more readily the left-hand species is reduced. Br2 (+1.07 V) is reduced more readily than I2 (+0.54 V), so Br2 takes electrons from I- and oxidises it to iodine. Cl2 (+1.36 V) is reduced more readily than Br2, so Cl- cannot give electrons to Br2; the reverse, chlorine oxidising bromide, is what occurs.

items: Half-cell types: metal/ion (Cu2+/Cu), non-metal/ion (Cl2/Cl-), ion/ion (Fe3+/Fe2+). Against the SHE: Cu2+/Cu +0.34 V (copper positive pole, Cu2+ easier to reduce than H+); Zn2+/Zn -0.76 V (zinc negative pole, Zn2+ harder to reduce).
Reduction at the positive terminal, oxidation at the negative terminal.
